title: The Garden of Junebug Creek
premise: August Brightwater inherited Junebug Creek Vineyard along with a mountain of debt and a family that treats reunions like audits. When her grandmother threatens to sell the land unless August proves she's 'settled,' August hires Delaney Voss — a traveling sommelier passing through town — to pose as her partner for one weekend. The fake romance turns devastatingly real, but Delaney is secretly in the valley to close a corporate acquisition of the very vineyard August is fighting to save. When the truth surfaces at the harvest festival, August must decide whether love is worth trusting again, and Delaney must choose between the promotion that defines them and the life they never planned. In the end, Delaney walks away from the deal, the family rallies to save the vineyard through a cooperative buyout, and the two plant a new varietal together on the hillside where they first kissed.
about_author: Mara Lockridge is the pen name of a former wine-country journalist who spent five years covering small-family-vineyard foreclosures before turning to fiction. She writes love stories set in places worth fighting for, from a farmhouse surrounded by test vines she pretends are ornamental.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: August's POV opens on a foreclosure notice pinned beside her grandmother's prize-winning rosé recipe. She catalogs what's left: forty acres, a failing tasting room, and $380,000 owed. The emotional beat is weary defiance — August has learned to treat hope as an expense she can't afford, establishing her guarded heart.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Grandmother Odette calls a family reunion for midsummer and delivers an ultimatum: bring someone real or sign the vineyard over to cousin Randall, who wants to flatten it into a resort. August, POV shifting between panic and pride, lies on impulse and claims she's seeing someone. The beat is reckless commitment to a lie.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Bar
chapters.summary: Delaney Voss arrives in Junebug Creek incognito, scouting the valley for the Meridian Group's acquisition team. At the town bar, they watch August get cornered by gossips and, on a whim, intervene — pretending to be her date. The beat is electric improvisation; two liars recognize each other instantly.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Over cold coffee at dawn, August offers Delaney room, board, and a cut of nothing, asking them to play her partner through the reunion. Delaney agrees, telling themselves it's good cover. Alternating POVs reveal both hiding something. The beat is a handshake built entirely on secrets.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: They practice their story in the vineyard rows: how they met, first kiss, favorite things. A staged kiss in the trellis shadows lands wrong — too real, too long. Delaney's POV shows the first crack in professional detachment. The beat is comedy curdling into want.

chapters.title: Arrivals
chapters.summary: The reunion begins. Randall circles with his lawyers; Aunt Pru interrogates Delaney over deviled eggs; Odette watches everything with sharp, unreadable eyes. August performs happiness so well it frightens her. The beat is performance under pressure, and the first genuine laugh shared between the leads.

chapters.title: The Blind Tasting
chapters.summary: Odette forces everyone into her annual blind tasting. Delaney's expert palate nearly exposes them — until they deliberately miss every answer to protect August's fiction, sacrificing credibility. August realizes the stranger just took a bullet for her. The beat is gratitude arriving disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: Night Swim
chapters.summary: Escaping the house party, August and Delaney swim in the creek under fireflies. Guarded truths slip out: August's dead parents, Delaney's rootless childhood. They almost kiss for real and retreat. Dual POV. The beat is intimacy outpacing the script.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: At the farewell dinner, Odette announces she believes them — and that she likes Delaney more than any grandchild deserves. Under the table, hands find hands and don't let go. By dessert, the fake relationship has become indistinguishable from the real thing. The beat is quiet surrender.

chapters.title: Staying On
chapters.summary: Neither will name why, but Delaney extends their stay 'to help with harvest prep.' Weeks pass in montage: pruning, arguments about terroir, Sunday dinners that feel like family. August's POV admits she's falling. The beat is domesticity as seduction.

chapters.title: Meridian on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Delaney's POV cracks open: their report recommending the Junebug Creek acquisition is due in three weeks, and their boss is pressing for signatures. Delaney stalls, editing the valuation upward to scare off buyers. The beat is guilt compounding into dread.

chapters.title: Randall's Offer
chapters.summary: Randall confronts August privately with Meridian paperwork — he's been brokering the sale all along. August, blindsided, fights him off but now knows a corporate buyer is circling. She tells Delaney, who says nothing. The beat is dramatic irony tightening like wire.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: The crew brings in the first real crop in years, and August and Delaney work side by side until midnight, then finally kiss without pretense in the crush pad. It feels like a beginning. The reader knows it's borrowed time. The beat is joy at its most vulnerable.

chapters.title: What Delaney Didn't Say
chapters.summary: A Meridian regional manager arrives unannounced, recognizes Delaney, and greets them by title in front of Pru. Delaney covers clumsily; August goes cold. That night August finds the draft acquisition report on Delaney's laptop. The beat is betrayal recognized in slow motion.

chapters.title: The Confrontation
chapters.summary: August demands the truth. Delaney confesses everything — the assignment, the stalled report, the feelings they insist are real. August, whose whole life is people choosing duty over her, cannot hear it. She orders Delaney off the property. The beat is heartbreak weaponized by old wounds.

chapters.title: Empty Rows
chapters.summary: August throws herself into harvest alone while the vineyard gossip mill churns. Odette, revealing she knew about the deception from day one, tells August that being loved imperfectly is still being loved. August refuses the lesson. The beat is grief wearing anger's clothes.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: In the city, Delaney faces the signed contract and the promotion that would erase their debts and define their career. They read August's one unanswered text — 'Was any of it true?' — and walk out of the meeting mid-signature. The beat is identity chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Meridian moves to close the acquisition in ten days; Randall produces a preliminary signature from a desperate Odette. August learns the cooperative buyout option exists but needs every family member's consent — including Randall's. The beat is the clock becoming the antagonist.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: At the town's festival, Delaney returns publicly, exposing Meridian's predatory terms to the whole valley using their own insider data. The crowd turns; Randall wavers. August watches the person who lied to her tell the truth at maximum cost. The beat is public reckoning.

chapters.title: Climax: The Vote
chapters.summary: The family convenes to vote on the cooperative. Randall, moved by Delaney's speech and Odette's quiet disappointment, abstains — enough to save the vineyard. But August, hurt still raw, tells Delaney saving the land doesn't mend them. The climax splits victory from forgiveness.

chapters.title: What Grows Back
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Delaney works the winter pruning as an employee, earning back trust row by row without asking for anything. August watches them fix the irrigation alone at dawn and understands Odette's lesson: love isn't a single grand gesture but repeated showing up. The beat is thaw.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Spring. On the hillside where they rehearsed their first fake kiss, August and Delaney plant a new varietal together — one that takes five years to bear fruit, a promise measured in patience. Odette approves; the found family gathers. The beat is love chosen freely, rooted deep, and finally home.
